title: Flow resume answers 200 and silently drops `variables` when the body also carries `inputs`
body:
Filing gate: ① product defect — reproduced through a public HTTP door, landing file named.
Path: automation.trigger-status-contract (checklist item priority P1; found while driving its steps[5], outside its clauses — no clause failed)
QA-source: #24545 · automation.trigger-status-contract · steps[5] (incidental, outside clauses)
Type: Bug — violates the resume route's own declared closed-set / no-silent-drop contract.
Reader: the `domain:cli` lane seat (owner of `packages/runtime`) — first step is the resume arm of `packages/runtime/src/domains/automation.ts` (~3197–3262).
Duplicate check (open AND closed): "flow resume body both inputs and variables, variables silently ignored" → 3 hits (#22642, #7639, #3853 — none match; #3853 is a different, closed resume-body hole) · "resume route variables alias inputs precedence dropped" → 1 hit (#3853, no match) · "resume body closed set unknown key inputs variables output branchLabel" → 0 hits.
reach: `POST /api/v1/automation/showcase_reassign_wizard/runs/RUN/resume` with both `inputs` and `variables` (the latter carrying an unknown screen field) → 200 `success:true`; the `variables` bag is never read. Measured on stock showcase at 5b14b7f3.

## What happens

The resume route accepts `inputs`, `variables`, `output` and `branchLabel` as a closed key set and type-checks each. When a body carries BOTH `inputs` and `variables`, the assembly reads `b.inputs ?? b.variables`, so `variables` is discarded without a word: the call answers 200 and the run completes, even when `variables` holds a field the screen does not declare. Sent alone, the same `variables` bag is judged (and refused) normally — so this is not a dead alias, it is a live key dropped only in combination.

## Reproduction (stock showcase, framework 5b14b7f3)

1. Boot showcase (`objectstack dev --seed-admin`), sign in `admin@objectos.ai` / `admin123` (`POST /api/v1/auth/sign-in/email`).
2. `GET /api/v1/data/showcase_task?limit=1&fields=id,assignee` → task id T.
3. `POST /api/v1/automation/showcase_reassign_wizard/trigger` body `{"recordId":"T","objectName":"showcase_task"}` → 200 `status:"paused"`, runId R, screen `collect` with required field `new_assignee`.
4. `POST /api/v1/automation/showcase_reassign_wizard/runs/R/resume` body `{"inputs":{"new_assignee":"inputs-win@example.com"},"variables":{"new_assignee":"variables-lost@example.com","bogus_key":1}}`.
   - Expected: a 400 refusal naming the conflicting keys (or, at minimum, the `variables` bag judged — which alone yields 400 INVALID_SCREEN_INPUT for `bogus_key`).
   - Actual: 200 `success:true`; the run completes; `GET /api/v1/data/showcase_task/T` shows `assignee: "inputs-win@example.com"`.
5. Controls (fresh paused runs): `{"variables":{"new_assignee":"v@example.com","bogus_key":1}}` → 400 INVALID_SCREEN_INPUT `Unknown screen field "bogus_key"`; `{"variables":{"new_assignee":"variables-only@example.com"}}` → 200 and the value is written.

## Contract

- `packages/runtime/src/domains/automation.ts:3135` — `variables` is in the accepted resume key set and is type-checked (~3231).
- `automation.ts:3152-3163` (closed-set note, commit a4331227b) and `:3197-3203` (value-shape note): the route states that silently dropping a submitted value while answering 200 is the defect family it closes.
- No published schema declares the resume body; the client SDK names only `inputs` / `output` / `branchLabel`, and `variables` is an undocumented accepted alias. The MCP `resume_run` door builds the signal from one source only, so it is not affected.

## Mechanism and fix landing

- `packages/runtime/src/domains/automation.ts:3259` — `const inputs = (b.inputs ?? b.variables);`
- Fix: refuse a body carrying both `inputs` and `variables` with the route's 400 validation-failure envelope (or merge and refuse on conflict) before `resume()`; pin it beside the existing closed-set / value-shape tests in `packages/runtime`.
- Severity hint: low — a caller has to send both keys; no data outside the caller's own run is affected.
